position_on: the key's financial-privacy side: opposing the creation of a U.S. central bank digital currency (CBDC) as a tool of financial surveillance, control of people's wallets, and a federal database standing between Americans and their rights
confidence_reason: Two posts on his own X account oppose a CBDC outright, one announcing his amendment to stop CBDCs as tools of financial surveillance and control of your wallet, and a 2023 House newsletter rejects central bank digital currencies alongside other federal databases; held at 0.75, below the 0.85 ceiling, because no press release or campaign page of his addresses CBDCs, cash or financial privacy, the House language lists CBDCs as one database among several, and the key's pole pairs financial privacy with crypto rules he does not speak to.

sources.excerpt: "BLOCKED: My amendment to stop the creation of Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) that will be used for financial surveillance and control of your wallet."
sources.note: Read directly on 2026-11-25 (full post text and timestamp, 2026-02-03T19:24Z, via X's public embed data; the trailing image link is left out). Part of his own thread listing amendments blocked from the February 2026 omnibus. His own words take a clear position against a CBDC. The amendment and any vote on the rule are not used as sources.

sources.excerpt: "You shouldn’t need permission from the Federal government to exercise your rights. This is why I oppose national databases such as: NICS, Real-ID, E-Verify, No-Fly-Lists, CBDC."
sources.note: Read directly on 2026-11-25 (full post text and timestamp, 2023-04-19T14:44Z, via X's public embed data; the line break before the list is collapsed here). His own words stating that he opposes a CBDC.

sources.excerpt: "In the Judiciary Committee, I explained that we do not need E-Verify, or other federal databases like NICS, Real ID, No-fly lists, and central bank digital currencies, in order for law-abiding Americans to exercise their fundamental human rights."
sources.note: Read directly on 2026-11-25. First-party newsletter from his House office, in the first person, under the heading "Rep. Massie on E-Verify: 'We Don't Need Another Federal Database'". This is the House-language source rejecting central bank digital currencies. CBDCs appear as one item in a list, which is one reason confidence is held below 0.85.

sources.excerpt: "'A rule requiring electronic ear tags will do to cattle and bison what central bank digital currency does to our dollar,' Massie told The American Conservative . 'The sale of animals can be monitored and blocked if farmers are not compliant.'"
sources.note: Read directly on 2026-11-25. First-party newsletter from his House office (the stray space before the period is as published). It is about livestock ear tags and uses a CBDC as a negative comparison for monitoring and blocking sales, so it is supporting evidence only, weighted weak.
